Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production pixel-art sprite sheet for a late-1990s tactical RPG.
Primary request: ONE original sprite sheet for Chai Jin, a noble hunter and swordsman from Water Margin, identifiable by rich deep-red and warm-brown hunting robes, a small high topknot, dark boots, and a one-handed straight sword. Use the attached local reference sheets only for the compact Jojo-era pixel art style and the portrait atlas for character identity.
Canvas/layout: exact 4 columns by 7 rows, 28 distinct FULL-BODY sprites, row-major, evenly spaced, no overlap, no grid lines, no captions. Transparent background. Logical cells 64x64 enlarged exactly 4x by nearest-neighbor, target full sheet 1024x1792. Center each character consistently; feet on same baseline within each cell. Keep entire sword and all body parts inside the cell.
Frame order by row:
row 1 columns 1-4: front-facing attack anticipation, deep windup with sword drawn back, extended full sword strike with visible weapon arc, recovery stance.
row 2: back-facing same four attack phases with visibly different silhouettes.
row 3: left-profile same four attack phases, with extended sword thrust/slash. Right profile will be mirrored by the game.
row 4: front walk step A, front walk step B, back walk A, back walk B.
row 5: left walk A, left walk B, front neutral, back neutral.
row 6: left neutral, hurt kneel, fallen on ground, front guard.
row 7: back guard, left guard, wounded recoil, victory raised sword or hand.
Actually 28 frames total: row 6 column 4 is frame 23 front guard; row 7 columns 1-4 are frames 24-27.
Style: original hand-drawn 1990s JRPG pixel art; compact 2.5-head stocky figure; hard square pixels and clean one-pixel dark outlines at logical resolution; limited flat palette, minimal dither, crisp readable sword; no smooth shading, gradients, antialiasing, blur, miniature rendering, 3D, painterly detail, text or scenery. Make all attack keyframes truly different, readable as a fast sword animation.
